annotations.text:
COMMUNITY — open-source AI your bots can use.

A new rail entry sitting directly above Machine, and the pairing is the point: Machine installs tools for you, Community installs them for your bots.

Five kinds of thing come through it — MCP servers (which become tools in the permission matrix), skills (written procedures), agents, models, and the runners that serve them.

Built on what DevDeck already is: tokens from src/index.css, the 160px rail with its 2.5px indigo bar, the 260px contextual sidebar, 12px panel radius, the 10.5/11.5/12.5 type ramp. Dark by default; every artboard has a light switch above it.

Static mockups, one direction.

THE ONE IDEA

Installing is not granting, and the module is built around that split.

An install writes files to disk. It gives no agent the ability to call anything — everyone lands on None. A separate, deliberate act says who may use it and how.

That is why there is an Installed page AND a Permissions page rather than one list with toggles: the second question is not a detail of the first, and the Installed page can then say the uncomfortable thing — supabase-mcp has been sitting there six days and no bot can reach it.

WHERE IT REFUSES TO FLATTER YOU

· "DevDeck does not review any of them." No stars-as-safety, no trust score. It reads a manifest and shows what the repo claims — and says a lying manifest looks clean.

· A failed source sync is a failure, not "up to date". Same bug the update checker once had.

· Licences are shown because they matter to a product that means to be sold: permissive, copyleft, restricted, or missing entirely.

· Model speed is measured on this machine, not lifted from a model card.

PERMISSIONS IS THE SPINE (artboard 4)

One table: community tools and built-in tools judged the same way, against every agent. Full / Read / Approval / None, exactly the four the runtime already has.

Built-in rows are on screen deliberately — a community tool is not a second-class citizen with its own weaker gate, it is a row in the same table.

Standing grants get their own panel because they are the only thing that can answer an Approval without you. Narrow, dated, revocable.

ARTBOARD 6 IS NOT A COMMUNITY PAGE

It is a feature thread — the one from node-thread — showing the module's whole reason to exist: qa asks, you answer, the tool runs, one call is refused for being outside the host you allowed.

The right-hand panel lists what came from Community and is in play right here. If that panel is ever empty for a real day's work, the module did not earn its rail slot.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR YOU

1 · Bundles are on Browse as a strip rather than their own page. Machine calls the same idea bundles, which is why the word is reused — but a Community bundle also carries grants, and that may deserve the fifth sidebar entry it currently has.

2 · Is Community its own rail entry, or a tab inside Machine? I put it on the rail because the audience is your bots, not your machine — but that is an argument, not a fact.

3 · Should an MCP server's process show up in Processes? Today it would not, and the Trust modal has to warn about exactly that.

SEVEN MODALS

Each one is a decision the module cannot make for you, and each answers with a receipt rather than a silent state change.

A · Install. Three questions: what it adds, where it lands (Personal, or the space's vault — never the repository), who may call it. Everyone starts at None.

B · The unvetted repo. No licence file, spawns processes, any host. It says outright that nothing was checked.

C · One cell of the matrix. The four permissions in the runtime's own words, plus the timeout that denies.

D · The update that widens what a tool can do. Four new write actions, so a Full grant is narrowed to Approval and the screen says why. A grant given against thirteen actions should not silently cover seventeen.

E · Sources. One has failed, and it is called failed — you are shown the timestamp of the last good copy instead.

F · Give it to a bot, with the announcement it will post in the bot's thread shown before you commit.

G · Pull a model — quantisation against free disk, what will not fit greyed out, and a reminder that weights are not a tool and have no row in Permissions.
